title: Late preschool care beyond 7pm and alternatives for parents who cannot collect their children in time
asked: Mr Gerald Giam asked how many preschools offer care beyond 7.00 pm on weekdays and whether that number has risen over five years, and what alternative care arrangements exist for parents without flexible work, domestic helpers or family support to pick up children by 7.00 pm.
response: Full-day preschools must operate 7.00 am to 7.00 pm on weekdays, and extending beyond that is left to operators; around 20 preschools now do so, down from 40 in 2021. The Minister pointed to flexible work arrangements, including the 2024 Tripartite Guidelines on FWA requests, and to paid and community-based options such as babysitting services. He said MSF and ECDA have no firm view either way on the suggestion of one extended-hours preschool per estate, and listed possible reasons for the fall in numbers, including lower demand, manpower constraints and a 2024 SG LEADS finding on long hours in preschool.

key_points.point: Full-day preschools are required to run from 7.00 am to 7.00 pm on weekdays.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: preschools providing full-day services are required to operate from 7.00 am to 7.00 pm on weekdays

key_points.point: About 20 preschools currently operate beyond 7.00 pm on weekdays, down from 40 in 2021.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Today, around 20 preschools operate beyond 7.00 pm on weekdays. This is a decrease from 40 preschools in 2021.

key_points.point: Extending operating hours is a business decision left to preschool operators, who may charge for the extra hours.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the decision to extend operating hours is a business decision that we have left to the preschool operators

key_points.point: Alternative care options for parents needing support outside standard hours include paid and community-based services such as babysitting.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: These include paid and community-based options, such as babysitting services.

key_points.point: The Tripartite Guidelines on FWA requests were launched in 2024, setting out how employees request flexible work and how employers consider it.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the launch of the Tripartite Guidelines on FWA requests in 2024

key_points.point: MSF and ECDA have no firm view either way on the suggestion of one extended-hours preschool per estate.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: I do not think ECDA or the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) will have a firm view either way on this.

key_points.point: A 2024 Singapore Longitudinal Early Development Study found effects on literacy and numeracy achievement when children stayed in preschool beyond 40 hours and significantly beyond.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the longer the children stayed in preschools, beyond 40 hours and significantly beyond, we start to observe that their literacy, their numeracy achievements do have some impact

left_open: Whether ECDA has carried out a proactive survey of actual parental interest in extended preschool hours.
Whether rigid preschool cut-off times affect lower- and middle-income parents differently.
